mainTopic: Who receives the injury payments when a father or others injure a daughter or son: רב's view that the Torah gave the father only שבח נעורים, and the challenges to it.
overview: רב rules that when someone injures a young daughter, the payment goes to her, because the Torah gave the father only שבח נעורים. רבי אלעזר objects from the עבד עברי and from a ברייתא that says others who injure a minor daughter pay her father. Both objections are answered: the father gets only שבת (lost work time), since her earnings are his. The גמרא then finds two ברייתות that disagree about a father who injures his own adult son. It settles them by asking whether the children are supported at his table. Defending that answer, it explains that a self-supporting daughter keeps what she needs for food and only the surplus goes to her father. It also explains that a supporting father lets his children keep injury money from outsiders, unlike a strict father who claims even that. Next the גמרא defines סגולה as a ספר תורה or a fruit-bearing date palm. Finally it brings ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן arguing over the same question and begins to challenge רבי יוחנן's view about a mere wound, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב: the father gets only the profits of her youth
steps.stepSummary: רב answers רבי אלעזר that the Torah gave the father only שבח נעורים, so injury money goes to the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: The Torah gave the father nothing except the profits of her youth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב is answering a question רבי אלעזר asked just before this: when someone injures a young daughter, who gets the payment? רב says the payment belongs to the daughter, not the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has certain special rights over his young daughter, called שבח נעורים. רב holds that the Torah limited the father to exactly those rights. Injury payments are not on that list, so they go to the girl herself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah granted (a right to someone)
Profits of youth: the father's special rights over his young daughter

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to him (Rabbi Elazar):
The Torah did not grant the father
anything except the profits of her youth alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא זִכְּתָה תּוֹרָה לָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question from the previous section of the daf.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Injury payments for a young daughter go to her, since the father's rights are limited to שבח נעורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father receives only שבח נעורים, so injury compensation belongs to the daughter.

steps.title: Objection from the Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר objects: a master who injures his עבד עברי is exempt from שבת, so a father should likewise keep his daughter's שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected to him: One who injures a Hebrew slave is liable for all the payments, except lost work time while the slave belongs to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges רב with a teaching about a Hebrew slave. When the owner injures his own slave, he does not pay for lost work time, because that lost work was his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave's work time belongs to the master, so the lost work is the master's own loss. A young daughter's work also belongs to her father. So at least the שבת payment should go to the father, and that seems to contradict רב's 'only שבח נעורים.'

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish (Hebrew) slave serving for a set term

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Elazar) raised an objection to him:
One who injures a Hebrew slave
is liable for all of them,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the five injury payments: damage, pain, healing, lost work, and embarrassment.

phrases.english: except for lost work time
during the time that he belongs to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the father gets nothing beyond שבח נעורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The person who owns someone's work time loses the שבת when that person is injured. The father owns his daughter's work, so he should get her שבת.

steps.title: אביי: רב agrees about lost work time
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רב agrees שבת goes to the father, since her earnings belong to him until בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רב agrees about lost work time, because her earnings until adulthood belong to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב by narrowing his statement. רב was never talking about lost work time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her earnings already belong to the father as part of his rights. So the payment for lost work time naturally goes to him. רב meant that the other payments, like pain and embarrassment, go to the daughter.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rav agrees regarding lost work time,
since her earnings until the time of adulthood
belong to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to give all the injury payments to the daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת goes to the father; רב's ruling covers only the other payments.

steps.title: Objection: others who injure her pay the father
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר cites a ברייתא that people who injure a minor daughter must pay her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: One who injures his adult son gives him the money right away; his minor son, he invests it safely for him. One who injures his minor daughter is exempt. Not only that, but others who injure her must pay her father!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a second challenge. A ברייתא says that when others injure a minor daughter, the payment goes to her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא seems to give the father the injury payments for his daughter in general. That clashes with רב, who said they go to the daughter. The father is exempt when he injures her himself, because the money would just come back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A safe investment (such as land) held for the child
And not only that, but even more

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
One who injures his adult son
must give him the payment immediately;
if he injures his minor son,
he must make a safe investment for him.
One who injures his minor daughter is exempt,
and not only that, but
others who injured her
are obligated to give the payment to her father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second objection to רב, after step 3 answered the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that injury payments go to the daughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says others who injure a minor daughter pay her father, which suggests all the payments belong to him.

steps.title: Here too, it means lost work time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers only to שבת, which goes to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too here, it is talking about lost work time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same idea אביי used. The ברייתא means only the lost work payment goes to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new principle is needed here. The father's right to שבת, already granted in step 3, explains this ברייתא too. The other payments still go to the daughter, just as רב said.

phrases.english: So too, it refers to lost work time.
phrases.notes: The words 'pay her father' in the ברייתא mean only the lost-work payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by applying אביי's answer from step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to give the father all the injury payments.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a minor daughter's injury payments go to her, except שבת (lost work), which goes to her father because he owns her earnings.

steps.title: Contradiction about injuring one's own adult son
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says a man who injures his own children is exempt, which clashes with 'he must pay his adult son immediately.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really pay his adult son immediately? A contradiction: One who injures the sons and daughters of others pays adults immediately and invests the money for minors. For his own sons and daughters, he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the first line of the earlier ברייתא, about a father who injures his adult son. It shows that a different ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says a father who injures his adult son must pay him right away. The second ברייתא says a father who injures his own children, apparently even adults, is exempt. Two teachings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against (another source): a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: And for his adult son, he must give him immediately?
And they raised a contradiction:
One who injures the sons and daughters of others:
if they are adults, he must give them the payment immediately;
if they are minors, he must make a safe investment for them.
If he injures his own sons and daughters, he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִבְנוֹ גָּדוֹל יִתֵּן לוֹ מִיָּד? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב's ruling to a contradiction inside the ברייתא quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a father who injures his adult son must pay him immediately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא exempts a father who injures his own children with no exception for adults.

steps.title: It depends on whether they eat at his table
steps.stepSummary: The father is exempt when the children depend on him for support, and he pays when they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It is not difficult. Here, when they are supported at his table; there, when they are not supported at his table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the adult children still depend on their father for food and support, he is exempt from paying them. If they support themselves, he must pay them like anyone else would. So the two ברייתות do not disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Dependent on his table: supported by him

phrases.english: They say: It is not difficult;
here, when they are dependent on his table,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the ברייתא that exempts the father.

phrases.english: there, when they are not dependent on his table.
phrases.notes: This one is the ברייתא that says he pays his adult son right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן כְּשֶׁסְּמוּכִים עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to conflict about a father injuring his adult son.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is exempt if the children depend on his support, and he pays if they are independent.
steps.whatToRemember: A father who injures his own child is exempt when the child is supported at his table, but must pay an independent adult child immediately.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'כאן's. The first (supported at his table) explains the exemption, and the second (not supported) explains why he pays.

steps.title: If the daughter is not supported by her father, why does her father collect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation that the first ברייתא is about children not supported by their father. Its סיפא says that others who injure a minor daughter pay her father, but a self-supporting daughter needs that money for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the first ברייתא? As talking about children who are not supported at their father's table? If so, look at its last part: one who injures his minor daughter is exempt, and others who injure her must pay her father. But if she supports herself, they should pay her, because she needs the money for food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the answer from step 7 and tests it against the last part (סיפא) of the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the first ברייתא is about children who are not supported by their father. The סיפא of that same ברייתא says that money for injuring the minor daughter goes to the father. That does not fit: a girl who has to feed herself should receive the money herself.

keyTerms.meaning: You explained it as being about (a specific case)
Supported at his table, meaning the father feeds them
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: How did you explain the first [ברייתא]?
As being where they are not supported at his table?
phrases.notes: This is the answer from step 7, which the גמרא is now testing.

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
One who injures his minor daughter is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲחֵרִים שֶׁחָבְלוּ בָּהּ –
phrases.english: and not only that, but others who injured her
must pay her father.
They should have to give it to her herself,
since she needs food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7 by checking how it works in the סיפא of the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that the first ברייתא is about children not supported by their father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A daughter who feeds herself needs the money for her own food, so it should not go to her father, yet the ברייתא gives it to him.

steps.title: Even a Hebrew slave must be fed, so surely a daughter must be
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes the question stronger. One view says a master may refuse to feed his slave, but that view applies only to an עבד כנעני. An עבד עברי must be fed, and a father's own daughter is all the more so entitled to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the one who says a master may tell his slave 'Work for me and I won't feed you' only says this about an עבד כנעני. The master can tell him: work all day, and at night go beg for food and eat. But about an עבד עברי the פסוק says 'for it is good for him with you,' meaning with you in food and with you in drink. If so, isn't it all the more so true of his own daughter?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a way out of its question. Someone might say a father does not have to feed his daughter, and the גמרא shows that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that the father may leave his daughter to fend for herself and still keep her injury money. The גמרא answers that the right to refuse food applies only to an עבד כנעני. An עבד עברי must be fed, and a daughter is all the more so (כל שכן) entitled to food, so she needs the money for her food.

keyTerms.meaning: Work for me and I will not feed you
A Jewish servant who works for a set term

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says:
a master can say to the slave,
'Work for me and I will not feed you';
that applies to a Canaanite slave,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: עֲבֵיד עֲבִידְתָּא כּוּלֵּי יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: because he can tell him: Do the work all day,
and at night go around and eat;
but a Hebrew slave, about whom it is written:
'For it is good for him with you':
with you in food, with you in drink;
is it not all the more so with his daughter?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the question of step 8 stronger by showing that a daughter must be fed.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense that the father may refuse to feed his self-supporting daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only an עבד כנעני can be left without food. An עבד עברי must be fed, so a daughter is all the more so entitled to food, and the injury money should cover her needs.

steps.title: The father gets only the surplus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers using רבא בריה דרב עולא's idea: the ברייתא gives the father only the העדפה, the money left over beyond what the daughter needs to live on.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא son of רב עולא said elsewhere: the rule is needed only for the surplus. Here too, the rule is needed only for the surplus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of steps 8 and 9 by borrowing an idea from another place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter does keep what she needs for food. The ברייתא's rule that others pay her father covers only the extra money beyond her needs (העדפה). So the explanation from step 7 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Surplus, money beyond what is needed to live on
This rule was needed only for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: The first ברייתא still fits children who are not supported by their father: the daughter keeps what she needs for food, and only the surplus goes to the father.

phrases.english: As Rava son of Rav Ulla said:
It is needed only for the surplus;
phrases.notes: He said this in כתובות 43a, about a daughter's extra earnings beyond what she needs to live on.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, לָא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְהַעְדָּפָה.
phrases.english: here too, it is needed only for the surplus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 8 and 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the ruling covers only the surplus.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the father collects all of the self-supporting daughter's injury money and leaves her without food.
steps.terutzMaskana: She keeps what she needs to live on, and only the surplus (העדפה) goes to her father.

steps.title: If the children are supported by their father, why don't they pay him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the explanation of the second ברייתא as being about children supported by their father. That ברייתא says adults are paid directly and money for minors is set aside for them, but if the father supports them, the money should go to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the second ברייתא? As talking about children supported at their father's table? But it says: 'Adults, give them the money right away; minors, set it aside in a safe investment for them.' Why? He should have to give it to their father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other half of step 7's answer and tests it against the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 placed the second ברייתא in a case where the children are supported by their father. If he supports them, the injury money should go to him. Yet the ברייתא pays adult children directly and saves the money for minor children, so the explanation looks wrong. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: A safe investment set aside for the children

phrases.english: How did you explain the latter [ברייתא]?
As being where they are supported at his table?
'Adults: he gives them the money right away;'
'minors: he makes a safe investment for them.'
Why? He should have to give it to their father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the first half of step 7's answer, the גמרא now attacks the second half.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that the second ברייתא is about children supported by their father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father feeds the children, the injury money should go to him. Yet the ברייתא pays the adults directly and saves money for the minors.

steps.title: A father only minds about money that would come from his own pocket
steps.stepSummary: The father insists on the money only when it would be a loss to him, as when he himself injured the child. Money that comes from outsiders he lets the child keep.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: A father cares about the money only when it would be his own loss. When the money comes from outside, he does not care.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. It explains why, even when the father supports his children, the injury money from outsiders goes to the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the father himself injures his child, paying would be a loss to him, so he insists on keeping it. When an outsider pays, the father loses nothing by letting the child have it, so he does not mind. This is why the second ברייתא sets the money aside for the children.

keyTerms.meaning: He is particular; he minds or insists on it
Causes a loss; something is lacking from him
From elsewhere, from the outside world

phrases.english: They say: When he is particular,
phrases.notes: "Particular" means the father insists on getting the money for himself.

phrases.english: it is in a matter that causes a loss,
but in a matter that comes from elsewhere,
he is not particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the father's likely attitude (his presumed wishes)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A supported child's earnings belong to the father, so injury money should go to him
steps.terutzMaskana: The father only claims money that would otherwise be his own loss; he gives up claim to money from outsiders

steps.title: But a found item also comes from outside, and the father takes it
steps.stepSummary: A מציאה also comes to the children from outside, yet the father keeps it. So the rule from Step 12 seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a found item comes to them from elsewhere, and still the father insists on taking it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 12. It points to a found object, which the father does take.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה is that a מציאה found by a child supported by his father belongs to the father. A found item costs the father nothing, since it comes from outside. So the idea that the father does not care about outside money seems to be contradicted.

phrases.english: But a found item,
which comes to them from elsewhere,
and he is particular!
phrases.notes: A child's found item goes to the father who supports him, so the father clearly does want outside money here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle given in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a father does not mind money that comes from outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מציאה comes from outside, yet the father keeps it, which contradicts the rule

steps.title: Injury money is different because the child suffered pain
steps.stepSummary: A found item is easy gain with no pain, so the father takes it. Injury money comes with the child's physical suffering, so the father lets the child keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Profit that comes from outside without any bodily pain, the father takes. But injury money, where the child suffered pain, even though it comes from outside, the father lets the child keep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge about a מציאה by adding a second condition: physical pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the father does not mind outside money, but that was not the whole picture. The father lets go only when the child also suffered in his body to get that money. With a found item there was no suffering, so the father feels the child did not earn it and takes it.

phrases.english: They say: Profit that comes to them from elsewhere,
and they have no physical pain in it,
he is particular;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֲבָלָה, דְּאִית לְהוּ צַעֲרָא דְּגוּפַיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: but an injury, where they have physical pain,
and it comes to them from elsewhere,
he is not particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by refining the rule of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the cases (adds a condition)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All outside money is treated the same, so a מציאה should go to the child
steps.terutzMaskana: The father lets go only of outside money that came with the child's physical pain, like injury money

steps.title: But the first ברייתא gives injury money from outsiders to the father
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא is about a daughter in pain whose money comes from outsiders, yet it says outsiders pay her father. That clashes with Step 14.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the first ברייתא, the daughter has bodily pain and the money comes from outside, yet the father insists on it! As it teaches: Not only that, but even others who injured her must pay her father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 14 using the סיפא of the first ברייתא, already quoted in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said a father does not take outside money that came with the child's pain. The first ברייתא says outsiders who injure the daughter pay the father, even though she suffered pain. So in that ברייתא the father does take such money, which seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָתָם, דְּאִית לַהּ צַעֲרָא דְּגוּפָא,
phrases.english: But there, where she has physical pain,
phrases.notes: "There" means the first ברייתא, the one about children not supported by their father.

phrases.english: and it comes to her from elsewhere,
and he is particular!
As it teaches: And not only that,
but (even) others who injured her
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: are obligated to give to her father!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָתָם, דְּאִית לַהּ צַעֲרָא דְּגוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the refined rule of Step 14 using the first ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a father does not take outside money that comes with the child's pain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first ברייתא gives exactly that kind of money (injury by outsiders) to the father

steps.title: The father in the first ברייתא is a strict man
steps.stepSummary: The father in the first ברייתא is a strict, demanding man, which is why his children are not supported by him, and he insists even on outside money. The father in the second ברייתא supports his children, so he is not strict and lets them keep outside money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, he is a strict man, as shown by the fact that his children are not supported at his table, so he insists even on money from outside. Here, he is not a strict man, as shown by the fact that his children are supported at his table. He insists only on money that would be his own loss, but money from outside he does not insist on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge by saying the two ברייתות describe two different kinds of fathers. This settles the whole question that began in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the father does not support his children shows he is a strict, demanding person, so he claims even outside money. A father who does support his children is generous, so he claims only money that would come out of his own pocket. This brings us back to the rule of Step 12, now limited to this kind of father.

keyTerms.meaning: Supported at his table; he feeds and supports them

steps.whatToRemember: A father who supports his children takes only money that would otherwise be his own loss, so injury money from outsiders goes to the children. A father who does not support them shows he is a strict man, and he takes even outside money.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a strict father has a stronger legal right. The גמרא is reading the ברייתא through the father's likely attitude, and his not supporting his children is the sign of that attitude.

phrases.english: They say: There, he is a strict man,
since they are not supported at his table,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בְּמִידֵּי דְּאָתֵי לְהוּ מֵעָלְמָא קָפֵיד.
phrases.english: so even in matters that come to them from elsewhere, he is particular.
Here, he is not a strict man,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the second ברייתא, where the children are supported by the father.

phrases.english: since they are supported at his table;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא קָפֵיד – בְּמִידֵּי דְּקָא חָסַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: when he is particular, it is in a matter that causes him a loss,

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִידֵּי דְּאָתֵי לְהוּ מֵעָלְמָא – לָא קָפֵיד.
phrases.english: but in a matter that comes to them from elsewhere, he is not particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 and closes the question opened in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the cases (different type of father in each ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות describe the same kind of father, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא describes a strict father who claims even outside money; the second describes a supporting father who claims only money that would be his own loss

steps.title: What is the safe investment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתות meant by סגולה, the safe investment the father makes for the children's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by a 'safe investment'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word סגולה means in the ברייתות. This short question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתות said the father should invest money that belongs to his young children. They did not say what kind of investment. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what the father should buy.

keyTerms.meaning: A safe, lasting investment kept for the child
What is it? A request to define a word

phrases.english: What is a 'safe investment'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling who keeps the money, the גמרא defines the investment the ברייתות mention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of investment is meant by סגולה

steps.title: A Torah scroll or a date palm
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the father buys a ספר תורה. רבה בר רב הונא says he buys a date palm that gives fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: a ספר תורה. רבה בר רב הונא says: a date palm that the child can eat dates from.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each one names a different kind of safe investment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא picks a ספר תורה, an item that keeps its value and can be used for learning. רבה בר רב הונא picks a date palm, which stays in place and gives the child fruit every year. Both answers are investments that keep the child's money safe.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says: A Torah scroll.
Rabba bar Rav Huna says:
A date palm from which he will eat dates.
phrases.notes: "He" is the child. He enjoys the fruit, and the tree itself stays as his property.

steps.whatToRemember: The children's money is not spent. It goes into something lasting, either a ספר תורה or a fruit-bearing date palm.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא: a ספר תורה. רבה בר רב הונא: a date palm that gives dates.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about the daughter's injury money
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the תורה gave the father only שבח נעורים. רבי יוחנן says the father gets even the money for a פציעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said ריש לקיש: The תורה gave the father only the profits of his daughter's youth. And רבי יוחנן says: even the money for a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about whether the father gets the money paid for his daughter's injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן ("and so") shows that this is the same question the גמרא was just discussing. ריש לקיש limits the father's rights to שבח נעורים, so injury money would go to the daughter. רבי יוחנן gives the father even the money for a פציעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The profits of a daughter's youth that the תורה gives her father
A wound, a bruise that does not lower her value
And so; the same issue is also discussed here

phrases.english: And so says Reish Lakish:
The Torah granted the father nothing
except the profits of youth alone.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Even a wound.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up פציעה and חבלה. A פציעה is a wound that does not lower her value. A חבלה is an injury that does lower it. The next step depends on this difference.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question of who gets the daughter's injury money and brings an argument about it from ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: the father gets only שבח נעורים. רבי יוחנן: the father gets even the money for a פציעה.

steps.title: Can the father really get money for a mere wound?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised at רבי יוחנן. Even רבי אלעזר only had a doubt about a חבלה, the more serious injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think the father gets money for a wound? Even רבי אלעזר only had a doubt about an injury...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement that the father gets even the money for a פציעה. The challenge continues past the end of this text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבלה lowers the daughter's value, so there is a reason to give its money to the father. Even so, רבי אלעזר was only unsure about the father getting money for a חבלה. A פציעה does not lower her value at all, so it seems far less likely that the father would get money for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A sign of surprise at a claim
He had a doubt about it, he asked about it
An injury that lowers the person's value

phrases.english: Does a wound enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: In other words: can you really think the father gets money for a wound that does not lower her value?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Even Rabbi Elazar raised his dilemma only
about an injury –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's view from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the father gets even the money for a פציעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר was unsure even about a חבלה, which does lower her value. So it is hard to say the father clearly gets money for a פציעה, which does not lower her value.
